1.q: הַ⁠דָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה
1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [7:1](ta:07).

1.q: אֶת פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת צְפַנְיָ֧ה בֶן מַעֲשֵׂיָ֛ה
1.note: The words **Pashhur**, **Malkijah**, **Zephaniah**, and **Maaseiah** are the names of men.

2.note: The word translated as **Please** here is a term used in polite requests. If it would be helpful for your readers, you could use an equivalent expression for making a polite request. Alternate translation: [We ask that you inquire of Yahweh on our behalf]

By **our**, Pashhur and Zephaniah mean themselves and the rest of the people of Judah but not Jeremiah, to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [on behalf of us and all our people]

2.q: כִּ֛י נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל נִלְחָ֣ם עָלֵ֑י⁠נוּ
2.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is fighting against us]

The implication is that **his wonders** are the miraculous deeds that Yahweh performed to rescue his people in earlier times. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [according to all the wonderful deeds by which he rescued us in the past]
The pronoun **he** refers to Nebuchadnezzar, not to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Nebuchadnezzar will withdraw from upon us]

Pashhur and Zephaniah are using the expression **he will withdraw from upon us** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he will break off the siege and go away.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will end the siege and leave us]

3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [You shall tell Zedekiah that]

The word **you** is plural here because Jeremiah is addressing both Pashhur and Zephaniah, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. This also occurs in verses 4, 8, and 12.

4.note: Jeremiah is using the expression **Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Yahweh is using **Behold me turning back** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he was about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to turn back]

4.q: אֶת כְּלֵ֣י הַ⁠מִּלְחָמָה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ⁠יֶדְ⁠כֶם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר
4.note: The word **your** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing King Zedekiah and his soldiers, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is speaking as if he were literally **turning back the weapons of war** that the people of Judah are holding. He means that he will make those weapons powerless against their enemies. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am making powerless the weapons of war]

4.q: וְ⁠אָסַפְתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֔⁠ם אֶל תּ֖וֹךְ הָ⁠עִ֥יר הַ⁠זֹּֽאת
4.note: The pronoun **them** could refer either to: (1) the weapons of war that Yahweh says he is turning back. Alternate translation: [and I will gather those weapons to the middle of this city] (2) King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian soldiers who are besieging the city. Alternate translation: [I will enable the king of Babylon and his soldiers to enter into the center of this city]

**Chaldeans** is another name for “Babylonians.” Both names occur often in this book. Decide as a team whether you will use the name “Babylonians” throughout the book or use the same name that is in the Hebrew text in each place, as the ULT does. Alternate translation: [and against the Babylonians]

5.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will fight** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is making a commitment to fight against Zedekiah and the people of Judah. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I will surely fight against you]

Here, **an outstretched hand** and **a strong arm** represent great power that is actively being used. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with great power actively displayed and with mighty strength]

The expressions **an outstretched hand** and **a strong arm** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two expressions together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [with my mighty power]

The terms **nose**, **heat**, and **great fury** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and with intense anger]

Yahweh is using the terms **nose** and **heat** as a common expression of the culture to mean “anger.” If these terms do not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and in anger]

6.note: The implication is that when Yahweh says that he will **strike the dwellers of this city**, he means that he will put them to death. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will strike down and kill the dwellers of this city]

Yahweh is referring to all of the living creatures in the city by naming two major components, **man** and **beast**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [every living creature there]

Yahweh is speaking as if he himself were **striking** the people of Jerusalem with a weapon, when he means that he will cause them to be killed by a plague. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will kill the dwellers of]

7.note: See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 10, 13, and 14.

7.q: וְ⁠אֶת הַ⁠נִּשְׁאָרִים֩ בָּ⁠עִ֨יר הַ⁠זֹּ֜את מִן הַ⁠דֶּ֣בֶר מִן הַ⁠חֶ֣רֶב וּ⁠מִן הָ⁠רָעָ֗ב
7.note: The implication is that **the ones remaining in this city** are the people who have survived **the plague**, **the sword**, and **the famine**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the ones in this city who have survived the plague, the sword, and the famine]

Here, **the hand** of Nebuchadnezzar represents his power and control. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [into the control of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon]

Yahweh is using the phrase **the seekers of their life** as a common expression of the culture to mean people who want to kill someone. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those hunting for their lives] or [those who want to kill them]
The pronoun **he** refers to Nebuchadnezzar, not to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Nebuchadnezzar will strike them to the mouth of the sword]

Yahweh is using the expression **strike them to the mouth of the sword** as a common expression of the culture to mean “kill them in battle.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he will kill them in battle]

7.q: לֹֽא יָח֣וּס עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וְ⁠לֹ֥א יַחְמֹ֖ל וְ⁠לֹ֥א יְרַחֵֽם
7.note: The terms **pity**, **spare**, and **have compassion** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [He will show them no mercy at all]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **compassion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he will not act compassionately]

8.note: The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Jeremiah, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

8.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֤י נֹתֵן֙ לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠כֶ֔ם אֶת־דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַ⁠חַיִּ֖ים וְ⁠אֶת־דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַ⁠מָּֽוֶת
8.note: **Behold me** is an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to give you the way of life and the way of death]

Here, **your faces** represents the people themselves, in whose presence Yahweh is setting these two ways. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before you]

8.q: אֶת דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַ⁠חַיִּ֖ים וְ⁠אֶת דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַ⁠מָּֽוֶת
8.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the two courses of action that the people may choose were **the way of life and the way of death**, that is, two roads leading to different destinations. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a choice between living and dying]

9.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what will happen to those who stay in the city and what will happen to those who leave it. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [In contrast, the one going out]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific person by the phrase **The one dwelling in this city**. He means anyone who stays in the city, in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone who stays in this city]

Yahweh is using the expression **falling upon the Chaldeans** as a common expression of the culture to mean “surrendering to the Chaldeans.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and surrendering to the Chaldeans]

Yahweh is using the expression **his life will be to him for spoil** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he will escape with his life and nothing else, as if his life were the only plunder he carried away from the battle.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will escape with nothing but his own life]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:12.

10.q: כִּ֣י שַׂ֣מְתִּי פָ֠נַ⁠י בָּ⁠עִ֨יר הַ⁠זֹּ֧את לְ⁠רָעָ֛ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א לְ⁠טוֹבָ֖ה
10.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [I say this because I have set my face against this city for evil and not for good]

Yahweh is using the expression **I have set my face against this city** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I have firmly determined to oppose this city.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have firmly determined to oppose this city]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **harm** and **good**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [to harm it and not to help it]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what will happen to the city before the information about who will receive it. Alternate translation: [it will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:4.

The expression **it will be given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will give it]
It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and he will burn it]

11.note: Here, **house** means all the people who belong to a particular person’s family. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of the king of Judah** figuratively means the king’s family and the royal officials who serve him. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And to the royal family of Judah]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.

This could mean: (1) And to the house of the king of Judah. Alternate translation: [Speak to the house of the king of Judah] or (2) And concerning the house of the king of Judah. Alternate translation: [Speak about the house of the king of Judah]

12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says to you, house of David, that you must]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **judgement** and **justice**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Judge justly in the morning]

The expression **is being robbed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one whom someone is robbing]

Here, **the hand** of the oppressor represents his power and control. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the power of the oppressor]

The word **lest** introduces the outcome that Yahweh wants the royal household to avoid, and obeying the commands that come before it is the way to avoid that outcome. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose of those commands.

The point of this comparison is that just as **fire** spreads quickly and destroys everything in its path, so Yahweh’s **wrath** will destroy the royal household if they do not obey him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [my wrath go out and destroy you as quickly and completely as fire burns]

Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of” or “on account of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on account of the evil of their deeds]

Even though Yahweh is addressing the royal household directly, he is speaking of them in the third person as **their** in the phrase **the evil of their deeds**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [the evil of your deeds]

13.note: Yahweh is using **Behold me against you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to oppose you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [See me turning against you] or [I am about to oppose you]

The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the city of Jerusalem as if it were a single woman, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is speaking of the city of Jerusalem as if it were a living person, a **dweller of the valley**, whom he could address directly. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you people who live in the valley]

Yahweh is speaking as if the city of Jerusalem were a **rock of the plateau**, that is, a height that no enemy could climb up to attack. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unassailable stronghold above the plain]

13.q: הָ⁠אֹֽמְרִים֙ מִֽי יֵחַ֣ת עָלֵ֔י⁠נוּ וּ⁠מִ֥י יָב֖וֹא בִּ⁠מְעוֹנוֹתֵֽי⁠נוּ
13.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [the ones saying that no one will come down upon them and no one will enter into their dwellings]

Even though Yahweh is addressing the people of the city directly, he is speaking of them in the third person as **the ones saying**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [you who say]

13.q: מִֽי יֵחַ֣ת עָלֵ֔י⁠נוּ וּ⁠מִ֥י יָב֖וֹא בִּ⁠מְעוֹנוֹתֵֽי⁠נוּ
13.note: The people of the city are using the question form to boast that no enemy is able to attack them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [No one will come down upon us, and no one will enter into our dwellings!]

14.note: The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing all the people of the city, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the expression **I will visit upon you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will punish you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will punish you]
See how you translated this expression in 17:10.

Yahweh is speaking as if the buildings of Jerusalem, which were constructed with great quantities of cedar wood, were **her forest**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will kindle a fire in her wooden buildings]

Yahweh is speaking of the fire as if it were a living thing that could **consume all her surroundings**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will destroy everything around her]
